the 60 (Cadrane) — desk dial

Projected from docs/v9/the60_v9/src/params.py + model.py (build123d) by hidden-line projection. No hand drafting; dimension text is written from the parameter values.
MODELLED, NOT PRINTED — no v9 part has been made. Dimensions are model values, not inspection results. Bodies tagged ENVELOPE or ASSUMED in the model are drawn as envelopes, not as the real part.
SECTION C–C scale 2.0 : 1
On the 90°–270° axis, clutch ENGAGED. Right of the centreline is the motor at 90°; the servo's inboard end crosses the centreline.
CL
r 40.50 motor axis
r 58.00 bore
14.00 motor
4.20 carriage
8.80 band
NOTES
The drive is friction, not gears: a Ø35 motor bell running on the Ø116 bore
through a 0.60 flat silicone band. Ratio 3.31 : 1. v8's gimbal drive and its
over-centre clutch are both gone.
JD-Power MY-3514C (2804), Ø35 × 14, on a carriage that slides radially in a
stadium hole through the plate. The carriage shoe is Ø37 on the pad, so the
motor's base face is at z 4.2 and its top at z 18.2.
The clutch IS the servo. An AGFRC C1.5CLS PRO linear servo (21.4 × 15.2 × 6
envelope) pushes the carriage tab directly; 2.40 of travel takes the bell from
contact to 2.40 clear. Preload — 2.4 N nominal — is a servo position set in
software, not a spring.
Commutation: an MT6701 on a 12 × 12 board inside the carriage, under the
motor, reading a Ø6 × 2.5 diametric magnet in the shaft's lower end through a
Ø9 sight hole. Which end of the shaft carries the magnet is ASSUMED. If it is
the top, this board moves and the display rises about 3 mm — over the 40 mm
height limit the specification sets, against 39.6 as modelled.
Not drawn, because nothing published says: the motor's bolt pattern (the
carriage has a Ø35.6 locating rim only), the servo's mounting lugs, and the
pushrod-to-tab joint. Measure all three on the real parts before printing the
carriage or the servo mount.
Band grip at 2.4 N is untested. If it slips under a firm hand, the fallback is
a 2 : 1 bell-crank between the servo and the tab — that doubles the force and
halves the travel, so the stadium hole would grow.
ENGAGED
0.60 band
RELEASED
DETAIL R — THE CLUTCH 4 : 1
Same section, same scale, 2.40 apart. Engaged, the band is squeezed 0.60 between
bell and bore. Released, the bell stands 2.40 clear and the knob free-spins.
The knob is never released by the wheels — only by the drive.
PLAN AT z 2.5 — INSIDE THE PLATE scale 0.78 : 1
carriage shoe on the pad
servo tray screws
port face
The stadium hole is the two carriage positions plus the slot
between them: Ø38.5 wide, r 18.9–59.8 at 90°, with a 10 × 10 tab slot reaching in to r 14.5.
The carriage rides on the pad, not on the plate.
PLAN AT z 13.4 — THE DRIVE BAND scale 0.78 : 1
Contact is a line at 90°, at r 58.00. Everything else on this level —
driver board at 152°, speaker, servo tray — stays outside the bell.
The wall relief is cut for the bell, 2.0 a side; the base below z 8.5 is narrower.
CARRIAGE AND SERVO TRAY — ISOMETRIC 1.9 : 1
The two printed parts of the drive, with the commutation board in its pocket. Motor and servo are left off: their envelopes hide everything that has to be made.
Assembly: board into the carriage, motor on top, band over the bell, servo into the tray, tray on the plate, then set the preload in software.
